claims.statement: `internal/architecture` is a test-only fitness boundary that collects only direct production import edges via `go list -json ./...` for module packages (`agent-harness/` prefix, trimmed by `normalizeImport`), deliberately excluding test imports and transitive dependencies so diagnostics stay precise `importer -> imported` pairs; the edge inventory is loaded twice and must be byte-stable (`reflect.DeepEqual`).

`evaluateEdges` enforces unconditional layer rules with no baseline — `core_must_not_import_adapter_or_cmd`, `adapter_must_not_import_cmd`, `port_must_not_import_internal`, `domain_must_not_import_implementation`, `application_must_not_import_implementation`, and `inbound_adapter_must_not_import_outbound_adapter` — over the entire production graph via `TestProductionGraphHasNoLegacyAdapterEdges`, and both rule names and diagnostic strings are pinned by `TestEvaluateEdgesRejectsForbiddenDependencies`.

The legacy-adapter baseline is zero and can only shrink: the baseline file `internal/architecture/testdata/legacy_imports.txt` was deleted (ratcheted from 263 edges to zero), `TestProductionGraphHasNoLegacyAdapterEdges` fails if `legacyEdges` returns anything, and a change removing a legacy edge must justify it in the same review; there is no registration path for new legacy edges.

`legacyEdges` classifies an edge as legacy (forbidden at zero tolerance) when: `internal/core/...` imports legacy infrastructure (`os`, `os/exec`, `net`, `net/http`, `database/sql`, `syscall`, anything containing `sqlite`); an adapter imports `internal/core/...` and is not one of the four migrated inbound adapters (`inbound/issueopslease`, `issueopspublication`, `issueopscompletion`, `issueopspreparation`); or a concrete adapter is imported from outside the composition root `cmd/harness/harnessapp`.

Capability boundary semantics (ADR 2026-08-08): a capability is the first path element after `internal/adapter/`, and `adapterCapability` reads one more element for `outbound`/`inbound` because they are direction classifiers, not capabilities; `isSameCapabilityAdapter` exempts same-capability adapter-to-adapter edges (package splitting is implementation cleanup, and counting them punished splitting with a bigger baseline, e.g. 226→181 when fixed), so only cross-capability concrete-adapter edges count as legacy.

The only canonical exceptions to 'adapters are imported solely by the composition root' are the shared storage primitives: `outbound/sqlstore` may be imported directly by any `internal/adapter/outbound/*` adapter and by `internal/adapter/issueops`, and `outbound/issueopsrecord` only by `internal/adapter/outbound/issueops*` adapters; `TestSharedStorageEngineExceptionIsOneDirectionOnly` proves the exception is one-directional (cmd, inbound, and domain code may not reach the engine) and must not widen, and new packages must not reuse these exception edges as a general bypass.

`evaluateOwnershipEdges` (exercised by `ownership_manifest_test.go`) applies stricter ownership rules: `ownership_forbids_core_package` bans the `internal/core/...` prefix on both importer and imported sides including the nested `internal/core/issueops/model` prefix (the core layer is dissolved and must not be reintroduced); contract/domain/port/application rules are scoped by the `isFoundationOwner` allowlist plus a package sweep for `issueops/model`.

Two vocabulary allowances are deliberate: ports speak contract vocabulary (`port -> contract` and `port -> port` are legal; only ports reaching domain/application/adapter/cmd fail, avoiding DTOs that no layer could own), and contract-to-contract references are contract composition rather than implementation coupling (`contract_must_not_import_internal` only fires for imports of domain/application/adapter/cmd/port), while vertical-specific stricter rules like `publication_contract_must_not_import_internal` remain in force.

Cross-capability adapter needs are satisfied by composition-root injection of function variables, not imports: consumer packages declare package-level `var X func(...)` slots in dedicated files (`adapter_dependencies.go`, `*_dependencies.go`, `adapter_tail_dependencies.go`), and the composition root assigns implementations in `cmd/harness/harnessapp/*_wiring.go` (e.g. `configurePolicyAndGitObservers` wires `policyadapter.EvaluateCommandPolicy` and `preflightadapter.GitCmd` into every CLI/adapter/MCP consumer), keeping implementation knowledge in exactly one place.

`cmd/harness/harnessapp/adapter_tail_wiring.go` owns the 'adapter tail' wiring: `configureAdapterTail` installs installation-planning and project-doc observation implementations (`installutiladapter`, `installadapter`, `projectdocsadapter`) into the host adapters (`claude`, `codex`, `omo`), the fingerprint adapter, and install/project leaf CLIs; it is one of ~30 `configure*` functions invoked in sequence by `wireBasicCLIDeps` in `cli_facade.go`, and the `gatesgate` package shows the same injection pattern for composition (`DiscoverGateFiles`/`CheckGateLedger` function variables instead of importing the gates adapter).

Two hard rules complete the injection pattern: dependency variables must have no default implementations (a default pointing at a concrete package recreates the edge; un-injected dependencies must fail closed with a structured error, never silently pass), and tests inject the same concrete implementations production wires — `harnessapp`'s `TestMain` calls `wireDependencies` to mirror `RunRootCommand` — while the fitness graph ignores test imports entirely.

`orphan_package_test.go` closes a blind spot of reachability-based dead-code analysis: `TestProductionPackagesHaveImporters` fails any non-main package with production Go files that no module package imports, because deleted wiring leaves tests green while enforcing nothing at runtime (the 2026-08-27 legacy-hook removal silently orphaned `internal/adapter/remoteartifact`, letting a wrong-target MR land); the remedy is reviving wiring or deleting the package.

The orphan allowlist is self-policing: `orphanPackageAllowlist` accepts only intended test-support packages, each with a written reason (e.g. `internal/adapter/skillcontract`, `cmd/harness/apidoc/dogfood`), and `TestOrphanPackageAllowlistHasNoStaleEntries` fails entries whose package no longer exists, has no production files, or has become imported — a stale entry would mask the next real orphan.

Migrated IssueOps capabilities carry focused vertical boundary tests: per-capability tests (`issueops_decision_vertical_test.go`, `issueops_inventory_vertical_test.go`, `issueops_retention_vertical_test.go`, `issueops_routing_vertical_test.go`, `issueops_status_vertical_test.go`, `issueops_artifact_vertical_test.go`) require the five-layer set (`contract`/`domain`/`application`/`inbound`/`outbound`) to exist, forbid vertical packages from importing the legacy `internal/adapter/issueops` root, and fail if legacy symbols or files reappear.

`issueops_record_store_test.go` requires six outbound IssueOps verticals (artifact, decision, inventory, retention, routing, status) to import the shared `internal/adapter/outbound/issueopsrecord` store and fails if duplicate record codecs (`codec.go`) reappear in individual verticals — the enforcement half of the `issueopsrecord` exception; `issueops_base_sync_boundary_test.go` separately restricts `internal/port/issueopsbasesync` to exported types `Request`, `Receipt`, `Inspector` and a single `context` import.

`documentation_test.go` keeps prose aligned with code: canonical documents (`README.md`, `README.en.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agent-harness/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.agent-harness/CONVENTIONS.md`, `architecture/hexagonal-core.md`, `conventions/go-and-packages.md`) must reference the current layer paths (`cmd/harness/`, `internal/contract/`, `internal/domain/`, `internal/application/`, `internal/port/`, `internal/adapter/`) and must not mention the removed paths `internal/core`, `internal/adapter/cli`, or `internal/adapter/fs`; first-party host docs must name Codex, Claude, and Omo.

Adjacent fitness tests in the same suite: `TestStateSQLNetworkSourcePrefixesAbsent` bans the dissolved `internal/core/{sqlstore,state,webfetch}` prefixes as packages and imports; `TestStateSQLNetworkImplementationImportsStayOutbound` forbids state/webfetch capability code outside `outbound/` from importing `database/sql`, `os`, `os/exec`, `net/http`, or sqlite; routing legacy-fallback tests require exactly one invocation of the injected handler per route and fail on legacy orchestration symbols (`PrepareExecution`, `ResumeExecutionWithDependencies`, `reconcileOrcaExecutionIntent`, `provider.Resolve` in publication callers); and production code must use `errors.AsType` instead of `errors.As`.

The prescription for removing a legacy edge is to classify the consumed symbol first: pure rules move to `internal/domain/<cap>`, types move to `internal/contract/<cap>` (field types cannot be replaced by injection), and I/O functions are injected from the composition root; type moves and function injection usually go together, and moving an edge upward (making a parent import an adapter after subpackage cleanup) reduces nothing.

Adding code without tripping the ratchet follows a fixed checklist with focused tests per change: any new/removed package runs `TestProductionPackagesHaveImporters`/`TestOrphanPackageAllowlistHasNoStaleEntries`; adapter imports run `TestProductionGraphHasNoLegacyAdapterEdges` and `TestLegacyEdges*`; touching `sqlstore`/`issueopsrecord` runs `TestSharedStorageEngineExceptionIsOneDirectionOnly`; foundation-package edges run the ownership manifest tests; new capabilities add a `<cap>_vertical_test.go`; doc/layer changes run `TestCanonicalArchitectureDocs`; and the full suite is `go test ./internal/architecture -count=1`, with failures reported as sorted `rule: importer -> imported` diagnostics.

The allowed dependency directions form an acyclic graph: the composition root (`cmd/harness/harnessapp`) imports inbound, outbound, and concrete adapters; inbound/outbound adapters call `internal/application`; application composes domain, port, and contract; domain and port import contract (and contract may import other contracts); the reverse directions (application/domain toward adapters or cmd, adapters toward cmd, inbound toward outbound, anything into `internal/core`) are rejected without a baseline.

Production runtime behavior, CLI/MCP response contracts, and runtime wiring are outside the ratchet's scope: the ratchet measures imports only, so moving a production package or reworking wiring does not require baseline changes unless an import edge changes; contract golden tests and the response-contract suite own the runtime surface, and host adapters added per the architecture docs add only a `port.HostInstaller` implementation plus composition-root wiring without duplicating domain/application policy.
